ABSTRACT: An organocatalytic enantio- and diastereoselective synthesis of hexahydropyrrolo[2,3-b]indole-containing
tetrasubstituted α-amino allenoates, exhibiting both axial and central chirality, has been accomplished via cascade
dearomatization−cyclization reaction. The γ-addition to β,γ-alkynyl-α-imino esters provides a library of densely substituted highly
enantioenriched allenes in high yields and excellent stereoselectivities. In addition, the scope of this methodology has been extended
to tryptophol as well. A scale-up reaction and synthetic transformations of the products were performed to demonstrate the practical
usefulness of this approach.
■
INTRODUCTION
The synthesis of enantioenriched heterocycles originating from
indole stands as a pivotal objective in both organic and
medicinal chemistry.
1
The hexahydropyrrolo[2,3-b]indole
(HPI) core represents a class of indole alkaloids, featuring an
all-carbon stereogenic center at the pseudobenzylic position.
The hexahydropyrrolo[2,3-b]indole ring having a carbon
substituent at the C-3a position is the defining structural
feature for a range of bioactive natural products and
pharmaceuticals including antifungal agent (I), antibacterial
activity (II), cholinesterase inhibitor (III), and neurokinin
antagonist (IV) (Figure 1).
2
Consequently, owing to the
structural complexity and promising medicinal value, the
synthesis of these heterocycles has drawn considerable
attention among synthetic chemists over the past decade.
3
In
this context, the frequently employed method for synthesizing
chiral HPI frameworks relies on catalytic asymmetric
dearomatization (CADA) of tryptamine derivatives, which
can utilize the C-3 nucleophilicity of the indole ring to attack
electrophiles (E) and initiate a cascade cyclization.
4
In the past decade, there has been a notable emphasis on
employing organoCADA of tryptamines with a diverse range of
electrophiles.
5−8
However, alkyne derivatives have rarely been
explored as electrophiles in the CADA reactions with
tryptamines. The latter class of reaction helps synthesize
HPIs containing an allene functionality at the C-3a position,
thereby introducing both axial and central chirality. Axially
chiral allenes are widespread and featured in many biological
natural products, functional materials, and important synthetic
intermediates.
9
Accordingly, considerable attention has been
directed toward exploring effective methodologies for synthe-
sizing densely functionalized allenic compounds.
10
Recently,
Shi et al.
11a
and Li et al.
11b
utilized para-aminophenyl
propargylic alcohols and α-(7-indolyl)propargylic alcohols,
respectively, as alkyne derivatives with tryptamines for the
asymmetric construction of axially chiral-tetrasubstituted
allenes bearing a HPI unit (Scheme 1a). However, poor to
moderate stereoselectivities were observed in most cases. Thus,
despite several efforts made, efficient asymmetric synthesis of
hexahydropyrrolo[2,3-b]indole bearing axially chiral tetrasub-
stituted allenes is still highly desirable.
Amidst various alkyne derivatives, β,γ-alkynyl-α-imino esters
are one of the most potentially useful and challenging

γ-addition) (Scheme 1b). Notably, direct α-addition to β,γ-
alkynyl-α-imino esters has been well explored for the synthesis
of optically active alkynyl α-amino acid derivatives.
12
In sharp
contrast, γ-addition of nucleophiles to β,γ-alkynyl-α-imino
esters has been rare. To date, 2,3-disubstituted indoles,
13a

were employed successfully for synthesizing
optically active amino allenoates. However, to the best of our
knowledge, the cascade dearomatization−cyclization reaction
with alkynyl ketimines as electrophiles has not been reported
in the literature so far and demands attention. This is probably
due to its formidable synthetic challenge, which includes (a)
controlling the regioselectivity in γ-addition rather than α-
addition and (b) controlling the diastero- and enantioselectiv-
ity in constructing HPIs bearing three contiguous stereogenic
centers.
In continuation of our work on Brønsted acid-catalyzed
enantioselective synthesis,
14
we became interested in exploring
organocatalytic asymmetric dearomatization (CADA)-initiated
ring closure reaction of tryptamines with β,γ-alkynyl-α-imino
esters leading to the formation of tetrasubstituted α-amino
allenoates containing an HPI unit (Scheme 1c). The
incorporation of two potent pharmacophore units, namely,
tetrasubstituted allene and pyrroloindoline, in a single chiral
molecule would be interesting in the context of drug discovery.
■
RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
To check the feasibility of our hypothesis, we initiated our
investigation by reacting β,γ-alkynyl-α-imino ester (1a) and N-
tosyl-protected tryptamine (2a), in the presence of 10 mol %
(R)-BINOL-derived phosphoric acid PA1 with 4 Å molecular
sieves (MS) in 1,2-dichloroethane at ambient temperature.
The corresponding adduct 3aa was isolated in 99% yield albeit
with 2:1 dr and 12% ee for the major diastereomer (Table 1,
entry 1). This preliminary result encouraged us to examine
other chiral phosphoric acid catalysts with different backbones
and steric environments (Table 1, entries 2−7). The optimal
result was obtained using anthracenyl-substituted BINOL-
derived catalyst PA5, as 3aa was isolated in 98% yield with
>20:1 dr and 91% ee (Table 1, entry 5). To further improve
the enantioselectivity, we turned our attention to optimize

Surprisingly, disubstitution on the phenyl ring in 1m resulted
in product 3ma with moderate enantioselectivity (82% yield,
85% ee, and >20:1 dr). The reaction proceeded smoothly
when the phenyl ring was replaced by a bulky naphthyl (1n) or
heteroaryl thienyl (1o) group, yielding 3na (85% yield, 93%
ee, and >20:1 dr) and 3oa (86% yield, 90% ee, and >20:1 dr),
respectively, in moderate yields with excellent stereoselectiv-
ities. Notably, the imino ester containing an alkenyl moiety 1p
readily underwent the reaction, to produce 3pa in good yield,
excellent diastereoselectivity, and moderate enantioselectivity
(81% yield, 83% ee, and >20:1 dr). In addition, the reaction
condition was also applicable with alkynyl ketimino ester
bearing COOMe substitution, producing the corresponding
product 3qa (92% yield, 94% ee, and >20:1 dr). In the case of
an alkyl substituent in 1r, product 3ra was obtained with
excellent stereoselectivity yet lower yield (56% yield, 95% ee,
and >20:1 dr).
The scope of the CADA−cyclization reaction was further
extended to various substituted tryptamines (2a−q), which
afforded a range of structurally diverse allene-substituted
pyrroloindolines (3ab−aq) in good to moderate yields (up to
93%) and excellent stereoselectivities (up to 97% ee and >20:1
dr) (Scheme 3). Representative N-tosyl-protected tryptamines
with either electron-withdrawing or electron-donating groups
at the 5-position resulted in smooth conversion and yielded
HPI derivatives (3ab−af) in moderate yields (62−84%) with
excellent stereoselectivities (87−95% ee and >20:1 dr).
However, in the case of 3af, with a Br group at the C-5
position, moderate yield and enantioselectivity were observed
(62% yield, 87% ee, and >20:1 dr). Tryptamines containing
different protecting groups were also tested in this protocol.
Variation of electronically and sterically diverse sulfonyl-
protecting groups (2g−p) revealed that the reaction condition
was well tolerated in most of the cases and the desired
products (3ag−ap) were obtained in low to good yields (45−
93%) and excellent stereoselectivities (90−97% ee and >20:1
dr). It was discovered that better enantioselectivity is realized
with aryl sulfonyls containing electron-donating groups rather
than electron-withdrawing groups. The best outcome was seen
in 3ao, having 2,4,6-iso-propyl substitution at the phenyl ring
(81% yield, 97% ee, and >20:1 dr). Nevertheless, in the case of
3am, the introduction of a highly deactivating NO
2
group
subsided the yield to 45%, although the stereoselectivity
remained excellent (91% ee and >20:1 dr). The reaction
protocol was also applicable with tryptamine bearing Boc
protection, producing the corresponding product 3aq (73%
yield, 94% ee, and >20:1 dr). In our attempt to extend the
scope of the methodology, tryptophol was also examined under
our optimized reaction conditions. The corresponding product
3ar with a furoindoline core bearing tetrasubstituted allene was
obtained in slightly lower yield, moderate enantioselectivity,
and excellent diastereoselectivity (66% yield, 87% ee, and
>20:1 dr).

CONCLUSIONS
In conclusion, we have developed a chiral Brønsted acid-
catalyzed enantioselective cascade dearomatization−cyclization
reaction of tryptamines with β,γ-alkynyl-α-imino esters. The γ-
addition to β,γ-alkynyl-α-imino esters led to the synthesis of
tetrasubstituted α-amino allenoates bearing a
hexahydropyrrolo[2,3-b]indole unit with both axial and central
chirality. The densely substituted highly enantioenriched
allenes were obtained in high yields and excellent stereo-
selectivities. Considering the presence of both tetrasubstituted
allene and HPI frameworks in a broad range of pharmaceuti-
cally potent molecules, we believe that the obtained products
will find application in different disciplines. The scale-up
reaction and interesting transformations further depict the
practical usefulness of this strategy.
■

General Procedure for Cascade Dearomatization−Cycliza-
tion Reaction. To an oven-dried round-bottom flask, equipped with
magnetic stir bar, β,γ-alkynyl-α-imino ester 1 (0.1 mmol, 1.0 equiv),
N-protected tryptamine 2 (0.12 mmol, 1.2 equiv), chiral phosphoric
acid catalyst PA5 (10 mol %), and 4 Å MS (100 mg), was added 1,2-
dichloroethane (2 mL). The reaction mixture was stirred at −10 °C
for 10 h. The reaction was monitored using TLC. After complete
consumption of starting material, mixture was concentrated in a rotary
evaporator and purified by column chromatography to afford pure
product 3.
Scale-up Reaction. To an oven-dried round-bottom flask,
equipped with a magnetic stir bar, β,γ-alkynyl-α-imino ester 1a (1
mmol, 1.0 equiv, 300 mg), N-tosyl-protected tryptamine 2a (1.2
mmol, 1.2 equiv, 377 mg), chiral phosphoric acid catalyst PA5 (10
mol %), and 4 Å MS (500 mg), was added 1,2-dichloroethane (10
mL). The reaction mixture was stirred at −10 °C for 12 h. The
reaction was monitored using TLC. After complete consumption of
starting material, the mixture was concentrated in a rotary evaporator
and purified by column chromatography to afford pure product 3aa
with 92% yield (566 mg).
General Procedure for Racemic Reactions. Racemic BINOL
phosphoric acid (10 mol %) was used for the synthesis of racemic
compounds. However, these compounds were obtained in moderate
yields. The racemic compounds were obtained as a mixture of
diastereomers. Some of the diastereomeric mixtures were inseparable
in silica gel column chromatography.
